protocol_name: Bulk omics from adherent cells: one cold acidified organic extraction, metabolome then proteome - module6_v1

sizing.capsule_count_note: not in chip spec; sheet default 100,000 used

events.narration: Neurons: load the lane's cell suspension through its own selector valve, filling the combs and field (one wetted volume), then stop flow so the cells settle and attach to the coated field floor. Held to the culture shear ceiling.

Glia: load the lane's cell suspension through its own selector valve, filling the combs and field (one wetted volume), then stop flow so the cells settle and attach to the coated field floor. Held to the culture shear ceiling.

Astrocytes: load the lane's cell suspension through its own selector valve, filling the combs and field (one wetted volume), then stop flow so the cells settle and attach to the coated field floor. Held to the culture shear ceiling.
All three lanes culture in parallel through their own ports: one wetted volume of fresh medium every interval at the shear-ceiling flow, then stop-flow. Durations are placeholders.

Neurons: brief ice-cold volatile-buffer rinse of 2 wetted volumes to waste, mandatory because the medium is about 150:1 against intracellular volume. Held to the 0.01 dyn/cm2 ceiling, so it is slow (12 min); a rinse-specific ceiling would cut it to seconds.

Neurons: quench flood in place, 2 wetted volumes in about 1 s through the combs, chloroform-free. Cells are lysed where they sit and the protein precipitates on the floor. The culture ceiling does not apply: the cells are killed. Outlet at waste, flow then stops.
Neurons: stop-flow extraction soak with the extract held cold. This is not a freeze-quench; the Peltier only keeps the extract cold.
Neurons: chase. The outlet valve is at vial M and fresh quench solvent pushes the extract (8.594 uL, about the pore volume plus a little) out through out_n.
Neurons: close vial M. FRACTION 1, the metabolome, plus peptides under about 10 kDa; neutralised on arrival, kept cold.

Neurons: the outlet valve returns to waste and 3 wetted volumes of solubilisation buffer clear the lane, port and stub of fraction 1 and displace the organic solvent. The precipitated protein stays on the floor.
Neurons: stop-flow resolubilisation of the precipitated protein on the chamber floor. It is denatured by design.
Neurons: chase. The outlet valve is at vial P and fresh buffer pushes the dissolved protein (8.594 uL) out through the SAME port out_n.
Neurons: close vial P. FRACTION 2, the proteome, ready for bottom-up digestion. The lane is spent; the transcriptome arm is separate and runs on capsules through module 4.
